newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: U.N. concerned over Vietnamese held in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. concerned over Vietnamese held in Cambodia.

text.p: Two United Nations agencies on Wednesday said they were concerned that a group of anti-Hanoi activists being held in Cambodia could be at risk if they are deported to Vietnam.
"We want to find out if they have something to fear if they are deported to Vietnam," Peter van der Vaart, chief of mission for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), told Reuters.
"If they face persecution, prison sentences or serious harm, they must not be returned," he said.
A representative of the U.N. Centre for Human Rights (UNCHR) said it was also concerned.

Immigration and police officials said on Wednesday that of the 24 men and four women, one would be deported to the U.S., an undisclosed number would be deported to Vietnam, and a few with Cambodian identity cards would be allowed to stay in Cambodia.

Co-Minister of Interior You Hokry told Reuters on Wednesday he had given permission for representatives of the two agencies to see the 28 detainees. but immigration officials said a time and date have not been set.

Government officials say they detained the 28 people, comprising one Vietnamese-American and 27 ethnic Vietnamese, for illegally trying to enter Thailand. They said the group belonged to the anti-Hanoi group, Tu Do Vietnam, or "Free Vietnam."
But rights officials say they understood that the 28 people are members of the People's Action Party, an anti-Hanoi group based in California.
Binh Si Nguyen, chairman of the People's Action Party, told Reuters from Thailand that the detainees were members of his party, which advocates democracy in Vietnam.
